'''Benjamin Franklin Finkel''' (July 5, 1865 – February 5, 1947) was a [[mathematician]] and educator most remembered today as the founder of the ''[[American Mathematical Monthly]]'' magazine.
== Life ==
Born in [[Fairfield County, Ohio]] and educated in small country schools, Finkel received both bachelor's and master's degrees from [[Ohio Northern University]], then known as Ohio Normal University (1888 and 1891, respectively).

In 1888 he copyrighted ''A Mathematical Solution Book''. The purpose of the book was to provide mathematics teachers a text utilizing a systematic method of problem solving, "The Step Method", representing a chain of reasoning, in logical order, to arrive at the correct result.<ref name=MathSolnBk>Benjamin Franklin Finkel (1899) [https://books.google.com/books?id=ugBDAAAAIAAJ ''A Mathematical Solution Book Containing Systematic Solutions to Many of the Most Difficult Problems'']</ref> The first edition was postponed until 1893, due to financial problems of the original publisher.<ref name=MacTutorHist>{{cite web|last1=O'Connor and Robertson|first1=J. J. and E. F.|title=Benjamin Franklin Finkel|url=http://www-history.mcs.st-andrews.ac.uk/Biographies/Finkel.html|website=The MacTutor History of Mathematics archive|publisher=School of Mathematics and Statistics University of St Andrews, Scotland|accessdate=22 January 2015}}</ref> The book's preface stated that the work was based upon eight years of teaching in the public schools.  Following editions were published in 1897, 1899 and 1902.<ref name=UPenBultn1908>[https://books.google.com/books?id=rNrOAAAAMAAJ ''University of Pennsylvania Bulletin,''] University of Pennsylvania (1908)</ref>

In 1895 he became professor of mathematics and physics at [[Drury University]], then known as Drury College. He was a University Scholar in Mathematics at the [[University of Chicago]] from 1895–1896.<ref name=UPenBultn1908 /> In 1906 he was awarded a doctorate from the [[University of Pennsylvania]], where he had earlier earned an additional master's degree in 1904 and a Harrison fellow appointment in 1905.<ref name=MacTutorHist />

He was a member of the [[American Mathematical Society]], 1891; the [[London Mathematical Society]], 1898; and [[Circolo Matematico di Palermo]], 1902.<ref name=UPenBultn1908 /> He retained his professorship at Drury College until his death in 1947.
